Companion Animal Travel Desk Routine Service Standards

This section sets out the daily standards for safe, courteous, and consistent handling of companion animal travel requests.

Staff on the Companion Animal Travel Desk must greet each traveler calmly, listen carefully, and confirm the animal's needs before any booking or boarding step is taken. The senior coordinator oversees daily service decisions, and staff must follow that guidance without delay when service issues, schedule changes, or special handling concerns arise. Every animal must receive patient attention from trained staff, and no one may rush an exchange when the animal appears unsettled, tired, or unwell. If a traveler asks for help with a pet such as Louie, the staff member must use clear language, remain respectful, and verify the necessary travel documents and carrier condition before proceeding.

The desk must keep work areas orderly, secure personal data, and ensure that records are entered with care so that animal details, traveler details, and service notes remain accurate. Staff must watch for hazards such as unsafe carriers, loose straps, wet floors, or signs of stress in an animal, and must report any concern to the safety coordinator at once. The safety coordinator reviews hazards and prevention, and staff are expected to support that review by describing what was seen, what action was taken, and whether further control measures are needed. When a situation is unclear, staff must pause the process and seek guidance rather than guessing or making promises to the traveler.

Communication at the desk must remain reassuring and professional at all times. Staff may explain general service steps, but they must not speculate about flight outcomes, animal reactions, or exceptions that have not been approved. Where coordination is needed with another department, the desk must pass along only confirmed information and keep the traveler informed in plain, courteous terms. If a traveler such as Rafael Johnson or Noah Shah needs special assistance, the same calm standard applies, with equal attention to safety, comfort, and documentation.

Any concern that cannot be resolved at desk level must be referred promptly to the senior coordinator or the safety coordinator for further direction.
